headline: Sellers Dominated Thursday as Broad Weakness Swamped All But the Most Defensive Corners
body_html:
Thursday's session closed with unmistakable pressure across the board. Of the 550 names in our coverage universe, 409 finished lower against just 135 gainers — a ratio that left little room for optimism. Homebuilders bore the sharpest pain, shedding 2.23% as a group, while Consumer names fell 1.63% and Materials dropped 1.43%. Healthcare and Software each shed more than 1%, underscoring how broadly the selling was distributed rather than confined to any single pocket of the market.

The lone sector to close in the green was Energy, edging up a modest 0.17% — a notable resilience given the day's otherwise uniform retreat. Semiconductors also held up better than most, declining just 0.30%, buoyed in part by standout individual performances from Marvell Technology, which surged 5.79%, and Qnity Electronics, up 5.93%. The outperformance in chip-adjacent names offered one of the few credible counternarratives to the session's dominant selling theme.

ScanSource was Thursday's most dramatic mover, rocketing 9.67% in a session that otherwise rewarded no sector category as a whole. On the downside, John B. Sanfilippo & Son slid 6.81% to lead decliners, with Cactus and STAAR Surgical each losing more than 6%. When the day's single best performer comes from distribution and not a high-momentum growth name, it tends to signal a market searching for footing rather than one ready to extend.

briefs.headline: Nordson Surges on Precision-Equipment Demand Signal
briefs.body: Nordson Corporation climbed 8.0% Thursday, making it the session's second-biggest gainer despite broad industrial-sector weakness that dragged the group down 1.05% overall. The divergence suggests investors may be selectively rewarding names with exposure to specialized manufacturing processes rather than broad industrial cyclicals.

briefs.headline: Geopolitical Pressure Builds Around Iran as Sanctions Escalate
briefs.body: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled that Washington intends to impose its most stringent-ever sanctions package on Iran, calling on China to participate in the effort. Separately, reporting indicated that Saudi Aramco routed at least four million barrels of crude through non-Hormuz shipping lanes to Chinese buyers, illustrating how energy supply chains are already adjusting to the elevated tension.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strike Claims Target Saudi Energy Infrastructure
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed attacks on Najran airport and Aramco facilities inside Saudi Arabia, adding a fresh flashpoint to an already unsettled Middle East picture. The development arrives as the U.S. simultaneously tightens its sanctions posture toward Iran, which has been linked to Hezbollah by fresh Treasury designations issued the same day.

briefs.headline: Pro-Sports Valuations Reach New Stratospheric Levels
briefs.body: Two major transactions underscored the accelerating inflation in North American sports franchises: the Los Angeles Lakers changed hands at a reported $12.5 billion, while private-equity firm Arctos agreed to acquire a 10% stake in the Atlanta Falcons at an implied $10.6 billion team valuation. Both deals reinforce how institutional capital continues to treat live sports rights as a premium asset class.

briefs.headline: CF Industries Stands Out as Agriculture-Chemical Bright Spot
briefs.body: CF Industries advanced 5.61% Thursday, one of the stronger moves in an otherwise punishing day for the broader Materials complex, which fell 1.43%. The fertilizer producer's outperformance may reflect expectations around crop-input pricing dynamics, though no specific catalyst was immediately attributed to the move in available reporting.

briefs.headline: Consumer Sector Takes a Broad Hit; Retail Names Lead Declines
briefs.body: Dick's Sporting Goods fell 6.25% and Ollie's Bargain Outlet shed 5.84%, helping pull the Consumer sector down 1.63% on the day. The weakness aligns with reporting showing U.S. sports fans spend roughly $2,000 annually supporting favorite teams, with many carrying debt as a result — a consumer-stress backdrop that may be weighing on discretionary retail sentiment.
